title: LLMs don't have Taste Buds
author: gorillasun

excerpt: I'm becoming increasingly aware that my neurodivergent ways of doing things might be a good reason why I'm not so easily replaceable by AI. Unfortunately, reasoning in a fundamentally different manner than the stochastic parrots is not something that I can simply include in my CV. I am also conscious that a vibe-based approach to things, as dirty as the connotations to the word have become today, does not necessarily foster the most consistent of practices. I recently saw this post by Bruce over on X, who you might better know as the creative mind behind Studio Yorktown, and felt personally called out: Bruce is an artist that I hold in high regard for his meticulous and discerning approach to creative work. From the projects I've seen him publish over the years, I have the impression that he is very structured and organised about everything that he does, not leaving much up to chance. Judging my own approach, I find that it sits at the other end of the spectrum. His post calls out something important that I don't do nearly enough—not with other people per se—but as a personal exercise where I put myself in the interrogation chair. Which I think is arguably much more difficult. And for a lot of personal creative work you can get away with a loose approach. While you will end up acquiring a sort of innate sense of "taste" and an abstract understanding for the "why"s, it's not a very tangible thing that can be easily described. If I had to put it into words, it's almost like a Marie Kondo-esque method (the KonMari Method™) for evaluating things based on the joy that they bring me. If I had to reason about every single step along the way, rather than following my desire to "see what could be", I would most likely be inhibited in my making of things. And it occurs to me that this might just be the reason why I've personally struggled working with agents in a creative setting, where you already need to have a hunch for what you want to achieve and then provide guidance…
